findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: In AccessTokenContext the constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId therefore passes validation and later produces a corrupt encoded id (e.g. prefix + ":null") or an NPE far from the source, while a null grantType produces a misleading message. Fail-fast validation is lost.

findings.title: Access-token-id matcher has inverted logic and wrong offset
findings.body: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId the check is if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false, which fails when the shortcut matches instead of when it mismatches. The offset is also wrong: grant shortcut is the last 2 chars of the 6-char prefix (indexes 4,6), not (3,5), which is second char of token-type plus first char of grant. There is no length guard before substring, so short ids throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The result is tests only verify colon+UUID and never verify the grant, giving false confidence.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut breaks existing grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds abstract String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory compiled against the old interface will throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut(), preventing server startup. It should be a default method returning the unknown value.

findings.title: grantType becomes stale after setFormParams
findings.body: In OAuth2GrantType.Context grantType is captured once in the constructor from formParams.getFirst(grant_type), but setFormParams() replaces formParams without updating grantType. If form params are mutated after construction, OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stores a stale GRANT_TYPE attribute and the encoded token id will contain the wrong grant.

findings.title: Removal of public Context copy constructor breaks callers
findings.body: The public constructor Context(Context) was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Existing custom grant code that copied the context via new Context(oldContext) no longer compiles. The copy constructor should be retained (and copy the new grantType field) or deprecated, not deleted.

findings.title: getShouldUseLightweightToken changed to static and can NPE
findings.body: AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken was changed from an instance package-private method to public static, which breaks any subclass that overrode it and changes polymorphic behavior. The body also dereferences session.getContext().getClient() without null checks, so callers with no ambient client (now including the token encoder) get an NPE instead of a safe default.

findings.title: Token context creation NPEs and uses wrong client for lightweight flag
findings.body: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext the code dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() with no null checks, so any context with null session fails token issuance with NPE. It also determines lightweight vs regular via the ambient session context client instead of the token's client from the ClientSessionContext, so when the ambient client differs or is null the encoded token-type disagrees with actual token content, causing downstream lightweight optimizations to read roles from the wrong place.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts not validated to be 2 chars without colon
findings.body: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit grant shortcuts are stored without validating length or content, while the encoder/decoder hard-codes a 6-char prefix (2+2+2) with ':' as separator. A custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returning a 3-char shortcut (as the javadoc even suggests) or containing ':' will encode to a prefix the decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException, breaking round-trip for that grant.

findings.title: Malformed token ids throw instead of returning UNKNOWN
findings.body: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId legacy ids without ':' return an UNKNOWN context, but any id with ':' and wrong prefix length or unknown shortcut throws IllegalArgumentException. Once this decoder is used on request paths like introspection/userInfo as the PR intends, attacker-controlled or foreign jti values will cause unhandled 500s instead of invalid-token handling. It should return UNKNOWN for forward compatibility.
